profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record sits at 1005 West Geneva Drive in Tempe, Arizona, within the Phoenix metropolitan area, tagged as a data center under the name Omnis Network. The name combines a common Latin derived business prefix with a direct reference to networking, a pattern often used by small internet service providers, managed network companies, or hosting operations, which would make a modest network services facility at this address plausible. A company called Omnis does have a public web presence, but it belongs to an unrelated software business based in the United Kingdom that develops cross platform application development tools, with no mention of Arizona, Tempe, or any physical network or data center facility. That company appears to be a coincidental name match rather than the operator of this Tempe address. No other website, business filing, or press coverage specific to Omnis Network at this location could be identified. Because the most obvious lead turned out to belong to a different, unrelated company, this entry does not attempt to describe Omnis Network's actual business in detail. It is published as an honest record of what is and is not confirmed about the Tempe facility, and will be revisited if a verifiable local operator is identified.

No AZ-specific Omnis Network domain could be reached. Cannot confirm operator.

reading.body:
Omnis Network in Tempe, Arizona is mapped as a data center but has no confirmed operator and no published power, floor space, or IT capacity, so it contributes nothing measurable to Arizona's known data center power total.

The name suggests a small hosting or network services operation, but the only public Omnis presence is an unrelated UK software developer, leaving the Tempe operator unverified. Arizona has 57 mapped data center facilities, and only four have published power figures, totaling 512 MW. This location is not among them, so it cannot be counted in the state's announced compute capacity.

The zero megawatt figure reflects missing data rather than measured consumption. Without operator confirmation or published specifications, the facility's size, activity, power draw, and role in Phoenix metro compute remain unknown, and it cannot be placed in Arizona's AI infrastructure trajectory.
